I've tried a lot of DEs in the past including Unity, KDE, XFCE, LXDE and even GNOME-3. I recently tried Ubuntu-MATE for the first time however, and found this to be the most efficient and complete DE experience.

I don't know whether its the DE itself or Ubuntu customizes it that way, but being a minimalist I like the following two qualities of this DE:

  1. No flashy animations or GUI bloat like you usually find in Unity or GNOME-3. I want a desktop that just works, nothing more or less. Things like the GNOME dash or Unity scopes (or stuff like Strigi/Akonadi in KDE) keep eating large chunks of your RAM like parasites and I don't like that.
  2. Yet, a truly complete Desktop! Unlike XFCE/LXDE/etc, MATE doesn't feel like a half-assed job done in the name of being "light-weight". It has all the features that GNOME-3 provides like the advanced Caja file manager which is based on Nautilus and fully featured utilities such as the MATE system monitor and Disks utility. Its also the little things that matter like the huge array of backgrounds and themes that come by default in a stock installation.

I think these two features make MATE a unique DE in its own right and there is no other DE that matches MATE in this regard.
I think MATE is the Number One Desktop Environment Linux has got

I've never been able to get into xfce either, I dont like thunar, I dont like the panel, I think mates allot easier to customize for me the way I like, though xfce is good too its just never felt right.
Would you recommend it for somebody who is a total Linux n00b and switching this weekend? I have years of experience programming, so I'm not afraid of the command prompt, or RTFM

Yes, totally recommend it. Once you start transitioning from a Linux n00b towards a Linux Pro, you'll start to understand that DE is just like a garnish on top of your GNU/Linux system, whereas the real work is done by the actual apps you use like bash, firefox, gimp, inkscape, etc. Given that, any Desktop should do and you can even install and try each of them out.

But for a first experience, I think MATE is pretty intuitive and easy to use, whether you are a former MAC or Windows user.
Cinnamon has allot of potential too, and is really great at the moment but could use more/ and better weather plugins and themes.

I'll paraphrase Linus' words from a while back about using GNOME (though I understand he uses GNOME himself nowadays): user-friendly desktop environments are so focused on making everything easy for the common person to use that I can't do the things that I want my computer to do. This is why I prefer KDE - sometimes even the right click menu has a right click menu inside it for customization. May sound like an exaggeration but as long as they're giving me the power to do whatever I want with my environment, I'll take it.

I think its extremely ironic that someone like Linus whose primary work involves linux and git which are exclusively developed and operated on the command line prefers a GUI instead to do the customizations! Linux and git, after all, are the very staples of the CLI world.

I'm sorry, maybe I expressed myself wrong. The only part referring to what Linus said some years ago is this one, the rest is my opinion:

user-friendly desktop environments are so focused on making everything easy for the common person to use that I can't do the things that I want my computer to do

From what I follow Linus has kept exclusively to the terminal until recently, most likely even reading e-mails and such via the command line. His use of GNOME is probably minimal, though he uses it nowadays - I imagine he mostly uses it as a way to have many terminals open at the same time and easier to manage than using different ttys and such. Who knows though, he could have started using other tools like graphical file managers, browsers and such. I guess that would make sense.
